title: United Airlines Worker Threatens to Call ICE on Mexican-American Citizen at SFO
excerpt: A viral video shows a United Airlines employee telling a naturalized U.S. citizen 'maybe we should call ICE on you' during a ticketing dispute at San Francisco airport.
body:
• A United Airlines employee at San Francisco International Airport told a Mexican-American U.S. citizen, "Maybe we should call ICE on you" during a ticketing dispute.
  • The employee also told Julio Varela, a naturalized citizen and San Ramon business owner, "You don't act like a citizen."
  • The confrontation, captured on video, went viral on Reddit and has drawn widespread condemnation as an example of racial profiling at airports.
  • United Airlines said it is investigating the incident but has not disclosed any disciplinary action.

What Happened

Julio Varela was trying to resolve a ticketing issue at San Francisco International Airport on Tuesday when a uniformed United Airlines employee escalated the exchange into a confrontation caught on camera. The 83-second clip, recorded by Varela, shows the employee telling him, "Maybe we should call ICE on you."

When Varela asked her to repeat herself, she doubled down: "Maybe you need to be, because you don't act like a citizen. Get away."

The dispute had started over a booking error — Varela's wife had accidentally entered their daughter's middle name in the last-name field. The family spent approximately 15 hours on the phone over two weeks trying to fix it. By the day of travel, the issue remained unresolved. Air Canada was able to rebook three family members but needed United to update the daughter's ticket first.

'I Am a US Citizen'

Varela, a Mexican-born naturalized U.S. citizen who owns a business in San Ramon, California, accused the employee of racism. "I am Mexican. I was born in Mexico. I am a US citizen. I own my own business. I pay taxes. I employ people," he told KQED.

"For her, especially with what's going on right now in America, to say that to a minority, especially a Hispanic person, I think it's really, really hateful and it's really racist."

— Julio Varela, passenger

The employee's badge identified her as a union steward with the International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers. Near the end of the clip, she stepped from behind the counter and reached toward Varela's camera.

A Broader Pattern

The incident comes during a period of heightened immigration enforcement at airports. Just days earlier, plain-clothes ICE agents attempted to arrest a passenger at Las Vegas's Harry Reid International Airport, drawing intervention from concerned onlookers. ICE has also made arrests at New York City immigration courts despite a federal judge's ban.

For immigrant communities — including the 4.5 million Indian-Americans, many of whom travel frequently between the U.S. and India — the weaponization of ICE threats by airline employees adds a new dimension of anxiety to air travel. Even citizens and legal permanent residents report feeling vulnerable in the current enforcement climate.

United's Response

"We're looking into the interaction in this video, but don't have anything additional to share at this time," United Airlines said in a statement. The airline has not disclosed whether the employee has been placed on leave or faces disciplinary action.

The incident echoes past controversies at United, which in 2017 faced global backlash after security officers dragged passenger David Dao from an overbooked flight in Chicago. That incident led to industry-wide policy changes on overbooking and passenger removal.
